fixed_commit_note: No post-incident source fix exists in this repo. The repository's final commit is dated 2022-08-04 (10+ months before the 2023-05-20 incident); the repo was never patched afterward. Governance control was restored off-repo via a subsequent re-vote (the attacker's proposal #21 resetting state), not by a Solidity source change. The design-level fix (not committing arbitrary delegatecall execution of CREATE2-mutable targets) was never applied here.
deployed_implementation: GovernanceStakingUpgrade (v3-relayer-registry), inheritance chain: GovernanceStakingUpgrade -> GovernanceGasUpgrade (v2) -> GovernanceVaultUpgrade (v2) -> Governance (v1). The vulnerable execute/propose/castVote/lock logic lives in the v1 Governance base and is inherited unchanged by the deployed v3 implementation behind the LoopbackProxy.

VULN-1_governance_seat_takeover.contract: Governance (v1) as inherited by deployed GovernanceStakingUpgrade (v3)
VULN-1_governance_seat_takeover.detail: By inflating their own lockedBalance voting power (see VULN-2) the attacker obtained an unassailable voting majority (~1.2M votes), passed and executed arbitrary proposals, and took de-facto control of the Governance contract / DAO.

VULN-2_vote_power_manipulation.detail: Vote weight is read directly from the lockedBalance[voter] mapping in _castVote and _propose. Because execute() runs the proposal via delegatecall in Governance's own storage context, the attacker's malicious executeProposal() body wrote fabricated entries into lockedBalance for addresses it controlled, assigning ~10,000 locked votes each (total ~1.2M) without ever locking TORN.

VULN-3_proposal_execution.detail: Root cause. execute() performs target.delegatecall(abi.encodeWithSignature("executeProposal()")) against a proposal target that passed only an Address.isContract() check. delegatecall grants the target full write access to Governance storage, and the target's code was mutable: the attacker deployed the approved proposal via CREATE2, selfdestructed it, and redeployed different (malicious) bytecode at the same approved address, so the executed logic differed from what voters reviewed.

technical_description: The deployed Tornado Cash Governance (v3 GovernanceStakingUpgrade behind LoopbackProxy, logic inherited unchanged from the v1 Governance base) executes passed proposals with target.delegatecall(executeProposal()), running attacker-supplied code directly against Governance's own storage after only an isContract check. The attacker deployed an approved-looking proposal at a CREATE2-derived address, got it voted through, then used selfdestruct + CREATE2 re-deployment to swap in malicious bytecode at that same address. On execute(), the malicious delegatecalled logic overwrote the lockedBalance voting-power mapping to grant the attacker ~1.2M fabricated votes, giving them majority control of the DAO; they later used that control to reset state via a follow-up proposal.
